sections.heading: Do British citizens need a Tanzania visa?
sections.text: British passport holders need a visa to visit Tanzania, including Zanzibar. You can apply online for an eVisa before travelling.

sections.heading: Tanzania visa for other passport holders
sections.text: UK residents on other passports usually apply the same way. Business and volunteering trips have their own visa rules.

sections.heading: Tanzania eVisa tips
sections.text: Apply well in advance, as processing can take longer in peak safari season. Check whether you need a yellow fever certificate, which depends on the countries you travel through.

sections.heading: Safaris, Kilimanjaro and Zanzibar
sections.text: If you're going on safari or climbing Kilimanjaro, your tour operator usually arranges park and climbing permits, but you still need your own Tanzania visa. The same visa covers mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar, so one application is enough for a combined trip. Make sure the dates on your application cover your whole stay, including any time on Zanzibar at the end of a safari.

sections.heading: Tanzania visa help from Manchester
sections.text: We're based in Manchester city centre and handle Tanzania visa applications for travellers across the UK, entirely online. We check the current rules for your nationality, complete your application and keep you updated until it's approved. Before you travel, read the UK government's [foreign travel advice](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice) for Tanzania.

faqs.q: Do British citizens need a visa for Tanzania?
faqs.a: Yes. You can apply online for a Tanzania eVisa before travelling.

faqs.q: Does the Tanzania visa cover Zanzibar?
faqs.a: Yes. Zanzibar is part of Tanzania, so the same visa covers it.

faqs.q: How long does a Tanzania visa take?
faqs.a: Usually a few working days, but processing times vary. Apply at least a week before you travel, and earlier in busy seasons.
